# Pidgeon

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c15 P25](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0025), [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044)</sub>
- **Role:** Teacher  <sub>[v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091), [v2 c4 P7](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0007)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mr.  <sub>[v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Teddy  <sub>[v1 c18 P6](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0006)</sub>

## Personality

Mr. Pidgeon is an extremely ineffective disciplinarian and teacher who constantly strikes his students yet maintains disgraceful discipline. He shows clear favoritism in the classroom, ignoring younger pupils and showing leniency to older students while spending extra attention on Sukey Pullen. At times, he displays sarcasm and spite toward students like Nell Harcourt, though he also demonstrates a romantic side and delivers a deeply emotional parting address to his school.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c15 P25](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0025), [v1 c15 P31](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0031), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091), [v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c19 P32](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0032), [v1 c20 P1](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0001), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v2 c4 P7](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0007)_

## History

Mr. Pidgeon served as the school teacher at Brierley school, where he was widely regarded as ineffective and maintained poor discipline. During his time teaching, he focused most of his efforts on older students preparing for the Regent's exams while neglecting younger children. He spent considerable attention courting student Sukey Pullen, helping her with algebra and Latin during class, giving her Mayflowers during a school outing, and visiting her home nearly every evening. He also dealt harshly at times with pupils like Nell Harcourt, publicly holding up her marked slate to criticize her spelling, making her stand on the dais, and forcing her to sit beside male classmates. Despite critics disparaging his abilities, he complimented Nell to Obed as the school's brightest student. At the end of his term, he delivered an emotional parting speech that brought himself and most of his female pupils to tears before leaving his post.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c15 P25](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0025), [v1 c15 P27](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0027), [v1 c15 P31](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0031), [v1 c15 P44](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0044), [v1 c15 P91](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0091), [v1 c18 P6](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0006), [v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c20 P1](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0001), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v2 c4 P7](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0007)_
